title: Royal burials concentrate at Meroe
summary: From the third century BCE, Meroe became the site of most royal burials in the kingdom of Kush. Pyramids and associated structures formed part of a larger urban and religious landscape.

claims.text: From the third century BCE, Meroe became the site of most royal burials in the kingdom of Kush. Pyramids and associated structures formed part of a larger urban and religious landscape.
The source dates this development to the third century BCE, not a particular year.

Kushite monuments place the Nile within an African history broader than Egypt alone. Their form can be compared with other burial traditions while keeping the distinct political and cultural setting visible.
